_description: Golden vectors for compressing a WebAuthn/P-256 (x, y) coordinate pair into the 33-byte SEC1-compressed point a MachineWallet authority slot stores. Read by BOTH repos so the two independent implementations — Swift `compressWebAuthnPublicKey` (soulpass-swift-sdk/Sources/SoulPassKit/Solana/WalletStateDecoder.swift) and TypeScript `compressP256` / `formatPasskeyPubkeyXY` (soulpass-ai/lib/machine-wallet.ts, lib/wallet-api.ts) — cannot silently drift apart. A drift here means an authority gets registered on-chain that nobody holds the matching private key for.
_generatedBy: Expected `compressed` values were produced with two mutually independent oracles, neither of which is the code under test: (1) Swift CryptoKit — `P256.Signing.PublicKey(x963Representation:).compressedRepresentation` and, for the scalar-derived point, `P256.KeyAgreement.PrivateKey(rawRepresentation: <32-byte-BE scalar>).publicKey.x963Representation`; (2) Python's `cryptography` library (OpenSSL-backed) — `ec.derive_private_key(scalar, ec.SECP256R1())` + `public_bytes(X962, CompressedPoint)`. Both oracles agreed byte-for-byte on every valid vector before this fixture was written.

valid.name: nist-p256-base-point-g
valid.note: The NIST P-256 base point G. G.y ends in 0xF5 (odd) so the compressed prefix must be 0x03. This is a well-known published constant, independently checkable against any P-256 reference.

valid.name: scalar-3-times-g
valid.note: 3*G, derived as scalar multiplication of the base point by the fixed small scalar 3 (reproducible: any P-256 implementation computing 3*G lands on this exact point). Chosen specifically because its y coordinate is even, so the compressed prefix must be 0x02 — the base point alone only exercises the 0x03 branch.

valid.name: base-point-g-0x-prefixed-input
valid.note: Same EC point as nist-p256-base-point-g, but both input coordinates carry a leading 0x/0X to exercise prefix-stripping. Expected compressed/xy outputs are identical to the unprefixed base-point vector — the prefix must be stripped, not treated as data.

invalidShape.name: x-coordinate-wrong-length
invalidShape.note: x is 31 bytes (one byte short of the required 32). Both a curve-aware compressor and a plain hex-shape formatter must reject this.
invalidShape.reason: x coordinate is 31 bytes, must be exactly 32

invalidShape.name: non-hex-coordinate
invalidShape.note: x has correct length (64 hex chars) but its last character is 'g', not a valid hex digit. Both a curve-aware compressor and a plain hex-shape formatter must reject this.

invalidCurve.name: off-curve-point-1-2
invalidCurve.note: (x=1, y=2), zero-padded to 32 bytes each. Correct length and valid hex, but does NOT satisfy the P-256 curve equation y^2 = x^3 - 3x + b (mod p) — verified independently via Python: (2*2) % p != (1 + (-3) + b) % p. A slot built from an off-curve point can never produce a verifiable signature; the caller who registers it loses access to that authority slot permanently. Only a curve-aware compressor is expected to catch this — a plain hex-shape formatter (right length, right alphabet) has no way to know.
invalidCurve.reason: (1, 2) is not a point on the P-256 curve
